name: Sasso Barisano
tagline: Restored cave district of boutique stays
description: The more restored of Matera's two Sassi, Sasso Barisano faces north and is lined with cave dwellings converted into boutique hotels, restaurants and artisan shops. Its polished stone lanes make it the most comfortable and atmospheric base within the ancient town.
bestFor: Travellers wanting boutique cave-hotel stays amid restored Sassi lanes

name: Sasso Caveoso
description: The older, more raw of the two Sassi, Sasso Caveoso tumbles toward the ravine with rupestrian churches, cave-house museums and dramatic viewpoints. Less commercialised than Barisano, it offers the strongest sense of Matera's original cave-dwelling past.
bestFor: History lovers wanting the most authentic ancient cave-dwelling atmosphere

name: Civita
tagline: Rocky heart between the two Sassi
description: The rocky spur crowned by Matera's cathedral, Civita is the oldest core rising between Sasso Barisano and Sasso Caveoso. Its narrow lanes and the panoramic Duomo terrace sit at the very centre of the ancient town, ringed by both cave districts.
bestFor: Visitors wanting the cathedral, viewpoints and a central Sassi position

name: Piano (Modern Town)
tagline: Flat upper town with everyday amenities
description: The modern upper city above the Sassi, centred on Piazza Vittorio Veneto and Via Ridola, holding most shops, banks, the train station and everyday services. Flat and practical, Piano suits longer stays and travellers wanting easy access without constant stairs.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting flat streets, shops and services near the Sassi
